    57	          ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0 (a + b) σ
    58	        = sectionCechProductEquiv (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)
    59	            ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0 a σ +
    60	          sectionCechProductEquiv (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)
    61	            ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0 b σ := fun a b => by
    62	    rw [sectionCechProductEquiv_apply, sectionCechProductEquiv_apply,
    63	      sectionCechProductEquiv_apply]
    64	    exact map_add _ a b
    65	  refine Eq.trans (hco _ _) ?_
    66	  -- piece 1: `π_{i_fix} ≫ ε` is `depDiff (depHomotopy t̃)` at the bottom level
    67	  have hpiece1 : sectionCechProductEquiv (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)
    68	      ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0
    69	      (ConcreteCategory.hom (cechSectionHomotopyZero 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV ≫
    70	        (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d 0 1) t) σ
    71	      = CombinatorialCech.depDiff (A := cechSectionCoeff 𝒰 F V) (cechSectionCoface 𝒰 F V)
    72	          (CombinatorialCech.depHomotopy i_fix (cechSectionPrepend 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV)
    73	            (fun τ => sectionCechProductEquiv (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)
    74	              ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0 t τ)) σ := by
    75	    refine Eq.trans (sectionCechProductEquiv_apply (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)
    76	      ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0 _ σ) ?_
    77	    refine Eq.trans (ConcreteCategory.comp_apply _ (Pi.π _ σ) _).symm ?_
    78	    refine Eq.trans (ConcreteCategory.congr_hom (Category.assoc
    79	      (cechSectionHomotopyZero 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV)
    80	      ((cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d 0 1) (Pi.π _ σ)) t) ?_
    81	    refine Eq.trans (ConcreteCategory.comp_apply _ _ t) ?_
    82	    refine Eq.trans (ConcreteCategory.congr_hom (sectionCechAugV_π 𝒰 F V σ)
    83	      (ConcreteCategory.hom (cechSectionHomotopyZero 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV) t)) ?_
    84	    refine Eq.symm ?_
    85	    refine Eq.trans (cechSectionDepDiff_zero 𝒰 F V _ σ) ?_
    86	    have htuple : ∀ ρ : Fin 0 → 𝒰.I₀,
    87	        cechSectionPrepend 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV 0 ρ
    88	          (sectionCechProductEquiv (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)
    89	            ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0 t (Fin.cons i_fix ρ))
    90	        = cechSectionPrepend 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV 0 Fin.elim0
    91	            (sectionCechProductEquiv (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)
    92	              ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0 t
    93	              (Fin.cons i_fix Fin.elim0)) := by
    94	      intro ρ
    95	      have hρ : ρ = Fin.elim0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
    96	      subst hρ
    97	      rfl
    98	    refine Eq.trans (DFunLike.congr_arg (cechSectionCoface 𝒰 F V 0 σ 0)
    99	      (htuple (σ ∘ (0 : Fin 1).succAbove))) ?_
   100	    refine DFunLike.congr_arg (cechSectionCoface 𝒰 F V 0 σ 0) ?_
   101	    refine DFunLike.congr_arg (cechSectionPrepend 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV 0 Fin.elim0) ?_
   102	    exact (sectionCechProductEquiv_apply (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)
   103	      ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0 t (Fin.cons i_fix Fin.elim0))
   104	  -- piece 2: `d⁰ ≫ h₁` is `depHomotopy (depDiff t̃)`
   105	  have hpiece2 : sectionCechProductEquiv (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)
   106	      ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0
   107	      (ConcreteCategory.hom ((cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d 1 2 ≫
   108	        cechSectionHomotopyComp 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV 0) t) σ
   109	      = CombinatorialCech.depHomotopy i_fix (cechSectionPrepend 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV)
   110	          (CombinatorialCech.depDiff (A := cechSectionCoeff 𝒰 F V) (cechSectionCoface 𝒰 F V)
   111	            (fun τ => sectionCechProductEquiv (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)
   112	              ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0 t τ)) σ := by
   113	    refine Eq.trans (congrArg (fun y => sectionCechProductEquiv (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)
   114	      ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0 y σ)
   115	      (ConcreteCategory.comp_apply _ _ t)) ?_
   116	    refine Eq.trans (cechSectionHomotopyComp_coord 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV 0 _ σ) ?_
   117	    exact DFunLike.congr_arg (cechSectionPrepend 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV 1 σ)
   118	      (cechSectionD_coord 𝒰 F V 0 t (Fin.cons i_fix σ))
   119	  refine Eq.trans (congrArg₂ (· + ·) hpiece1 hpiece2) ?_
   120	  refine Eq.trans (CombinatorialCech.depHomotopy_spec i_fix (cechSectionCoface 𝒰 F V)
   121	    (cechSectionPrepend 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV)
   122	    (fun {m} σ' y => cechSection_hu 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV σ' y)
   123	    (fun {m} σ' k y => cechSection_hsh 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV σ' k y)
   124	    (fun τ => sectionCechProductEquiv (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)
   125	      ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0 t τ) σ) ?_
   126	  exact congrArg (fun y => sectionCechProductEquiv (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)
   127	    ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0 y σ)
   128	    (ConcreteCategory.id_apply t).symm
   129	
   130	/-- The coinductive step: given the previous homotopy condition, the corrected component
   131	`h_{n+2} ≫ (𝟙 - p₂₁ ≫ d)` satisfies the next one (pure preadditive algebra from `(In)`
   132	and `d ∘ d = 0`). -/
   133	private lemma cechSection_succ_step (n : ℕ)
   134	    {f : (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).X (n + 1) ⟶ (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).X n}
   135	    {g : (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).X (n + 2) ⟶ (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).X (n + 1)}
   136	    (hp : 𝟙 ((cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).X (n + 1)) =
   137	      f ≫ (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d n (n + 1) +
   138	        (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d (n + 1) (n + 2) ≫ g) :
   139	    𝟙 ((cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).X (n + 2)) =
   140	      g ≫ (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d (n + 1) (n + 2) +
   141	        (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d (n + 2) (n + 3) ≫
   142	          (cechSectionHomotopyComp 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV (n + 1) ≫
   143	            (𝟙 ((cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).X (n + 2)) -
   144	              g ≫ (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d (n + 1) (n + 2))) := by
   145	  have hIn := cechSection_comm_succ 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV n
   146	  have hsub : (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d (n + 1) (n + 2) =
   147	      (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d (n + 1) (n + 2) ≫ g ≫
   148	        (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d (n + 1) (n + 2) := by
   149	    have h₀ := congrArg (fun m => m ≫ (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d (n + 1) (n + 2)) hp
   150	    simpa only [Category.id_comp, Preadditive.add_comp, Category.assoc,
   151	      HomologicalComplex.d_comp_d, comp_zero, zero_add] using h₀
   152	  have hd1E : (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d (n + 1) (n + 2) ≫
   153	      (𝟙 ((cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).X (n + 2)) -
   154	        g ≫ (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d (n + 1) (n + 2)) = 0 := by
   155	    rw [Preadditive.comp_sub, Category.comp_id, sub_eq_zero]
   156	    exact hsub
   157	  have hdb := eq_sub_iff_add_eq.mpr ((add_comm _ _).trans hIn.symm)
   158	  rw [← Category.assoc ((cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d (n + 2) (n + 3))
   159	    (cechSectionHomotopyComp 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV (n + 1)) _, hdb, Preadditive.sub_comp,
   160	    Category.id_comp, Category.assoc, hd1E, comp_zero, sub_zero]
   161	  abel
   162	
   163	end ContractingHomotopy

   165	set_option maxRecDepth 8000 in
   166	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
   167	set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
   168	-- Coinductive homotopy packaging has deeply nested dependent degree equalities.
   169	/-- The concrete augmented section Čech complex is contractible after choosing a cover member
   170	that contains `V`. -/
   171	noncomputable def cechSection_contractible (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) [Finite 𝒰.I₀]
   172	    (F : X.Modules) (V : TopologicalSpace.Opens X)
   173	    (i_fix : 𝒰.I₀) (hiV : V ≤ coverOpen 𝒰 i_fix) :
   174	    Homotopy (𝟙 ((sectionCechComplexV 𝒰 F V).augment (sectionCechAugV 𝒰 F V)
   175	      (sectionCechAugV_comp_d 𝒰 F V))) 0 :=
   176	  -- The prepend-`i_fix` contracting homotopy on the augmented concrete section complex,
   177	  -- assembled by `Homotopy.mkCoinductive` from the explicit components (`π_{i_fix}` at the
   178	  -- augmentation node, prepend-`i_fix` in the Čech degrees) and the three contracting
   179	  -- identities (I0)/(I1)/(In) proved above via the dependent combinatorial engine.
   180	  Homotopy.mkCoinductive _
   181	    (cechSectionHomotopyZero 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV)
   182	    ((HomologicalComplex.id_f _ _).trans (cechSection_comm_zero 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV))
   183	    (cechSectionHomotopyComp 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV 0)
   184	    ((HomologicalComplex.id_f _ _).trans (cechSection_comm_one 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV))
   185	    (fun n p =>
   186	      ⟨cechSectionHomotopyComp 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV (n + 1) ≫
   187	          (𝟙 (((sectionCechComplexV 𝒰 F V).augment (sectionCechAugV 𝒰 F V)
   188	              (sectionCechAugV_comp_d 𝒰 F V)).X (n + 2)) -
   189	            p.2.1 ≫ ((sectionCechComplexV 𝒰 F V).augment (sectionCechAugV 𝒰 F V)
   190	              (sectionCechAugV_comp_d 𝒰 F V)).d (n + 1) (n + 2)), by
   191	        have hp := (HomologicalComplex.id_f _ _).symm.trans p.2.2
   192	        exact (HomologicalComplex.id_f _ _).trans
   193	          (cechSection_succ_step 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV n hp)⟩)
   194	
   195	end AlgebraicGeometry

name: task-status
description: What the task status labels mean and how you (the agent) set them — you OWN your task's terminal status via `horizon task set`; the machine only ever leaves it queued/running, so `done` is never inferred from your report or a clean exit.
---

A task is the unit of work a run dispatches. **You own its outcome.** The
orchestrator/scheduler only ever writes `queued` and `running`; it never reads
your report and never marks a task `done`, `blocked`, or `failed` for you. If you
do not record a terminal status, the task simply returns to `queued` for the next
round. Record status through the CLI — invoke it via the `$HORIZON_BIN` env var
(an absolute path); a bare `horizon` may not be on your shell's PATH.

## The labels

- `queued` — runnable. The scheduler picks up only queued tasks. This is where a
  task rests between rounds when work remains. **Set by the machine (and humans);
  you normally don't.**
- `running` — a session is actively driving it right now. **Set by the machine at
  dispatch.** Don't set this yourself — it means "another session is live," and
  the CLI refuses to start a second run of a `running` task.
- `done` — the assigned objective is **FULLY complete**: the Lean is proved and
  builds, the blueprint node(s) are closed, nothing in the objective remains. Not
  "mostly done", not "the hard part is done", not "a clean commit landed". **Only
  you can set this, and only when it is genuinely, completely finished.** A
  reviewer (human or work-reviewer subagent) checks it against the diff and the
  Lean state and will flip a premature `done` back — so a false `done` wastes a
  round, it doesn't save one.
- `blocked` — you cannot make progress: a dependency is missing, a decision is
  needed, or an external constraint stops you. Say why in a comment.
- `failed` — you genuinely could not do the work (not merely "ran out of time" —
  that's just `queued` for next round). Say why in a comment.
- `cancelled` — abandoned by a human. You won't normally set this.

## How to set status

```
"$HORIZON_BIN" task set <task_id> --status done      # objective FULLY complete
"$HORIZON_BIN" task set <task_id> --status blocked   # stuck; explain in a comment
"$HORIZON_BIN" task set <task_id> --status failed    # could not do it; explain
```

Authorship is automatic — the CLI stamps your role (normally `horizon`) from the
run environment; do not pass `--author`. Setting a status appends an auditable
history entry, and if the task has `roadmap_refs` the linked roadmap items are
synced (done→done, blocked/failed→blocked, cancelled→rejected).

Task commands also report advisory queue-health warnings. Review an oversized
open queue for duplicated or roadmap-only objectives, and investigate a task
that has remained `running` past the stale-status window. These warnings never
change status for you; if the state is intentional, it may remain as-is.

## Comment as you work

Leave a short comment whenever you hit a significant step or change the status, so
the ledger tells the story without opening raw logs:

```
"$HORIZON_BIN" task comment <task_id> --body "Closed the base case; representability lemma still open."
```

## The one rule to remember

**If the objective is only partly advanced, set nothing.** The task returns to
`queued` and the next round continues it. Reserve `done` for work that is
completely finished — that is the entire point of the status now living with you
instead of being guessed from your report.

\chapter{Codimension-1 indeterminacy extension (A.4.a)}
\label{chap:Albanese_CodimOneExtension}

This chapter isolates two codimension-one inputs to the extension theorem for rational
maps.  A rational map from a normal variety to a complete variety is defined away from a
closed subset of codimension at least two, while a map to a group variety has indeterminacy
that is either empty or purely codimension one.  We also record the equivalent
Weil-divisor obstruction in terms of orders along prime divisors.
The depth-\(\geq 2\) reduction uses
\cref{cor:regular_cohen_macaulay} from
\cref{chap:Albanese_AuslanderBuchsbaum}, and the two codimension-one outputs
feed the extension theorem in \cref{chap:Albanese_Thm32RationalMapExtension}.

\section{Setup and motivation}
\label{sec:codim1_setup}

Fix an algebraically closed field \(\bar k\) throughout. By a \emph{variety} over \(\bar k\)
we mean a geometrically integral, separated scheme of finite type over \(\bar k\)
(Milne's convention, \emph{Abelian Varieties}, p.~v); a variety is \emph{nonsingular}
(or \emph{smooth}) if its local ring at every closed point is regular. A variety is
\emph{complete} if it is proper over \(\bar k\).

A \emph{rational map} \(f \colon X \dashrightarrow Y\) between varieties is the equivalence
class of a regular morphism \(\varphi_U \colon U \to Y\) defined on a dense open subset
\(U \subseteq X\), where two pairs \((U, \varphi_U)\), \((U', \varphi_{U'})\) are equivalent
if \(\varphi_U\) and \(\varphi_{U'}\) agree on \(U \cap U'\) (Milne~\S I.3, p.~16). The map \(f\)
is \emph{defined at} a point \(x \in X\) if there is some representative \((U, \varphi_U)\)
with \(x \in U\); the set of such \(x\) is an open subset \(\mathrm{Dom}(f) \subseteq X\),
the \emph{domain of definition} of \(f\).

The motivating question of this chapter, following Milne~\S I.3, is:
\begin{quote}
  \emph{When does a rational map \(f \colon X \dashrightarrow Y\) extend to a regular
  morphism on all of \(X\)?}
\end{quote}
Without hypotheses on \(X\) or \(Y\) the question has no positive answer (Milne lists three
counterexamples on p.~16: the inclusion of a proper open into the ambient variety; the
rational map to the cuspidal cubic whose inverse fails to extend; the inverse of a
blow-up at a smooth point). The two structural inputs that buy unconditional extension
in our setting are:
\begin{itemize}
  \item \emph{Target completeness:} if \(Y\) is complete (proper over \(\bar k\)), the
    valuative criterion of properness forces the rational map to extend across every
    codim-\(1\) point of a normal source \(X\) (Milne Theorem~3.1).
  \item \emph{Target group structure:} if \(Y\) is a group variety, the difference map
    \(\Phi(x, y) := f(x) \cdot f(y)^{-1}\) on \(X \times X\) has a vanishing/pole divisor
    along the diagonal that controls the codimension of the indeterminacy locus
    (Milne Lemma~3.3).
\end{itemize}
For \(Y\) an abelian variety both conditions hold, and combining them yields Milne's
Theorem~3.2 (the headline of \cref{chap:Albanese_Thm32RationalMapExtension}). The
present chapter packages the two inputs separately:
\cref{thm:codim_one_extension} is Milne~3.1, and
\cref{lem:milne_codim1_indeterminacy} is Milne~3.3. The Weil-divisor reformulation
\cref{thm:weil_divisor_obstruction} translates the codim-\(1\) extension obstruction
in Milne~3.1's proof into the order-at-a-prime-divisor language pinned in
\cref{chap:RiemannRoch_WeilDivisor}.

\section{The indeterminacy locus of a rational map}
\label{sec:indeterm_locus}

\begin{definition}


\leanok
  [Indeterminacy locus of a rational map]
  \label{def:indeterminacy_locus}
  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.RationalMap.indeterminacyLocus}
  % SOURCE: [Milne, Abelian Varieties], \S I.3, p.~16, the paragraph "Let \(V\) and \(W\)
  % be varieties over \(k\)\ldots" defining the domain of definition of a rational map
  % (read from references/abelian-varieties.pdf, PDF page 22).
  % SOURCE QUOTE: "A rational map \(\varphi\) is said to be \emph{defined} at a point
  % \(v\) of \(V\) if \(v \in U\) for some \((U, \varphi_U) \in \varphi\). The set \(U_1\) of
  % \(v\) at which \(\varphi\) is defined is open, and there is a regular map
  % \(\varphi_1 \colon U_1 \to W\) such that \((U_1, \varphi_1) \in \varphi\) --- clearly,
  % \(U_1 = \bigcup_{(U, \varphi_U) \in \varphi} U\) and we can define \(\varphi_1\) to be
  % the regular map such that \(\varphi_1 | U = \varphi_U\) for all $(U, \varphi_U) \in
  % \varphi$."
  \textit{Source: Milne, \emph{Abelian Varieties}, \S I.3, p.~16.}
  Let \(f \colon X \dashrightarrow Y\) be a rational map between varieties over \(\bar k\).
  The \emph{domain of definition} of \(f\) is the open set
  \[
    \mathrm{Dom}(f) \;:=\; \bigcup_{(U, \varphi_U) \in f} U \;\subseteq\; X,
  \]
  i.e.\ the union of the dense opens of all representatives of \(f\). The
  \emph{indeterminacy locus} of \(f\) is the closed complement
  \[
    Z(f) \;:=\; X \smallsetminus \mathrm{Dom}(f) \;\subseteq\; X.
  \]
  The map \(f\) is regular (i.e.\ defined on all of \(X\)) if and only if \(Z(f) = \emptyset\).
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}\leanok
[Indeterminacy locus is closed]
  \label{lem:isClosed_indeterminacy_locus}
  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.RationalMap.isClosed_indeterminacyLocus}
  \uses{def:indeterminacy_locus}
  For any rational map \(f \colon X \dashrightarrow Y\) of schemes, the
  indeterminacy locus \(Z(f) = X \smallsetminus \mathrm{Dom}(f)\)
  (\cref{def:indeterminacy_locus}) is a closed subset of \(X\): it is the
  complement of the open domain of definition \(\mathrm{Dom}(f)\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
  The domain of definition is open, and the complement of an open subset is closed.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}


\leanok
  [Codimension-1-indeterminacy-free rational maps]
  \label{def:codim_one_indeterminacy}
  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.RationalMap.CodimOneFree}
  \uses{def:indeterminacy_locus, def:prime_divisor}
  % SOURCE: [Milne, Abelian Varieties], Theorem~3.1, \S I.3, p.~16 --- the conclusion
  % "an open subset \(U\) of \(V\) whose complement \(V \smallsetminus U\) has codimension \(\geq 2\)"
  % is the standing predicate we abstract (read from references/abelian-varieties.pdf,
  % PDF page 22).
  % SOURCE QUOTE: "A rational map \(\varphi \colon V \dashrightarrow W\) from a normal
  % variety \(V\) to a complete variety \(W\) is defined on an open subset \(U\) of \(V\) whose
  % complement \(V \smallsetminus U\) has codimension \(\geq 2\)."
  \textit{Source: Milne, \emph{Abelian Varieties}, Theorem~3.1, \S I.3, p.~16 (the
  conclusion).}
  Let \(f \colon X \dashrightarrow Y\) be a rational map between varieties over \(\bar k\).
  We say \(f\) is \emph{codim-1-indeterminacy-free} (or has \emph{codimension-\(\geq 2\)
  indeterminacy}) if every irreducible component of the closed subset \(Z(f) \subseteq X\)
  has codimension \(\geq 2\) in \(X\). Equivalently, no prime divisor of \(X\) is contained in
  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.RationalMap.mem_domain_iff_exists_partialMap_through_point}
  Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be varieties over \(\bar k\) and let
  \(f \colon X \dashrightarrow Y\) be a rational map. For a prime divisor
  \(W \subseteq X\) with generic point \(\eta_W = W.\mathrm{point}\), the
  following are equivalent:
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item \(\eta_W \in \mathrm{Dom}(f)\) (\(f\) is defined at the generic point of
      \(W\)).
    \item There exists a partial-map representative \((U, \varphi_U)\) of \(f\) ---
      i.e.\ a regular morphism \(\varphi_U \colon U \to Y\) on a dense open
      \(U \subseteq X\) whose induced rational map equals \(f\) --- whose domain
      \(U\) contains \(\eta_W\).
  \end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}

  By definition, \(\eta_W\in\mathrm{Dom}(f)\) precisely when some
  representative of the rational map is defined on an open neighbourhood of
  \(\eta_W\).  Such a representative gives (2), and conversely the domain of
  the representative in (2) witnesses membership in \(\mathrm{Dom}(f)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
  \label{rmk:mem_domain_partial_map_reshuffle_scope}
  \textbf{Relationship to \cref{thm:weil_divisor_obstruction}.}
  \cref{lem:mem_domain_partial_map_reshuffle} captures the definitional half of
  the equivalence: a partial-map representative exists through the generic point
  of the prime divisor. The additional mathematical input in
  \cref{thm:weil_divisor_obstruction} is the identification of the local ring with
  the nonnegative part of the associated discrete valuation, applied to the
  pullbacks of regular functions on an affine neighbourhood of the image.
\end{remark}

\section{The codimension-one method}
\label{sec:codim1_lean_encoding}

The results above form a short chain of local and global arguments:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item Smoothness makes every codimension-one local ring a discrete
    valuation ring (\cref{lem:smooth_codim_one_dvr}).
  \item Properness and the valuative criterion then rule out
    codimension-one indeterminacy (\cref{thm:codim_one_extension}).
  \item For a group-variety target, the difference map and its pole
    divisors force every nonempty indeterminacy locus to be pure of
    codimension one (\cref{lem:milne_codim1_indeterminacy}).
  \item For a prime divisor, regularity is equivalently the absence of
    negative order in every pulled-back affine coordinate
    (\cref{thm:weil_divisor_obstruction}).
\end{enumerate}
Thus a rational map from a nonsingular variety to a complete group variety
has empty indeterminacy locus: it has no codimension-one component by (2),
whereas (3) says that every nonempty indeterminacy locus has such a component.

\section{Relations with neighbouring results}
\label{sec:codim1_out_of_scope}

The regular-implies-Cohen--Macaulay theorem
\cref{cor:regular_cohen_macaulay}, obtained from Auslander--Buchsbaum in
\cref{chap:Albanese_AuslanderBuchsbaum}, gives a depth-theoretic description
of the same regular local rings.  The valuative proof of
\cref{thm:codim_one_extension} does not require that stronger description.

Combining \cref{thm:codim_one_extension} and
\cref{lem:milne_codim1_indeterminacy} gives Milne's Theorem~3.2,
\cref{thm:rational_map_to_av_extends}.  Its later rigidity consequences
use the group structure after the extension has been obtained.

The divisor argument needs only the decomposition
\[
  \div(h)=\div(h)_0-\div(h)_\infty
\]
and the codimension-one support of principal divisors.  It does not use the degree of a divisor on a curve or
intersection numbers on a surface.  Cartier divisors could be substituted
for Weil divisors on a smooth variety, where the two theories agree.

The algebraically closed base guarantees that closed points have residue
field \(\bar k\).  Over a general field, the local statements persist after
accounting for residue-field extensions, while descent of the resulting
global morphism is a separate question.

/-- **(I1)** The augmentation-node contracting identity:
`𝟙 = π_{i_fix} ≫ ε + d⁰ ≫ h₁` on `Č⁰`. -/
private lemma cechSection_comm_one :
    𝟙 ((cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).X 1) =
      cechSectionHomotopyZero 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV ≫ (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d 0 1 +
        (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d 1 2 ≫ cechSectionHomotopyComp 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV 0 := by
  ext t
  apply (sectionCechProductAddEquiv (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)
    ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0).injective
  funext σ
  refine Eq.symm ?_
  have hsplit : ConcreteCategory.hom
      (cechSectionHomotopyZero 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV ≫ (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d 0 1 +
        (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d 1 2 ≫ cechSectionHomotopyComp 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV 0) t
      = ConcreteCategory.hom (cechSectionHomotopyZero 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV ≫
          (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d 0 1) t +
        ConcreteCategory.hom ((cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d 1 2 ≫
          cechSectionHomotopyComp 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV 0) t := by
    rw [AddCommGrpCat.hom_add_apply]
  refine Eq.trans (congrArg (fun y => sectionCechProductAddEquiv
    (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V) ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0 y σ)
    hsplit) ?_
  refine Eq.trans (congrArg (fun y => y σ)
    (map_add (sectionCechProductAddEquiv (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)
      ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0) _ _)) ?_
  -- piece 1: `π_{i_fix} ≫ ε` is `depDiff (depHomotopy t̃)` at the bottom level
  have hpiece1 : sectionCechProductEquiv (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)
      ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0
      (ConcreteCategory.hom (cechSectionHomotopyZero 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV ≫
        (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d 0 1) t) σ
      = CombinatorialCech.depDiff (A := cechSectionCoeff 𝒰 F V) (cechSectionCoface 𝒰 F V)
          (CombinatorialCech.depHomotopy i_fix (cechSectionPrepend 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV)

      "body": "Recipe: building ModuleCat-R morphisms into sheaf-of-modules section objects (v4.31) \u2014 the ConcreteCategory.ofHom + presheaf-obj pattern, and the let-fvar IsIso gotcha\n\nLanded in `tildeIso_of_isQuasicoherent_isAffineOpen` (`QuotScheme.lean`, T12 run 0010). When you need `f : ModuleCat.of R M \u27f6 <sections object>` (e.g. to feed `tilde.map`):\n\n- **Target the honest `ModuleCat R` object** `(modulesSpecToSheaf.obj G).presheaf.obj (Opposite.op \u22a4)` \u2014 this is literally the domain module of Mathlib's `fromTilde\u0393`/`toOpen`. Do NOT target `moduleSpec\u0393Functor.obj G` via `ModuleCat.ofHom`/`\u2192\u2097` type ascriptions: elaboration whnf-unfolds the carrier past `restrictScalars`, and `Module R <unfolded carrier>` synthesis then fails (no refold; a letI at the folded form does not match either).\n- **Construct via `ConcreteCategory.ofHom { toFun := ..., map_add' := ..., map_smul' := ... }`** with the expected hom type ascribed \u2014 the instances come from the objects via the `(\u00b7 \u2192\u2097[R] \u00b7)` FC family, no synthesis. A bare `let blin : M \u2192\u2097[R] <object> := ...` fails; skipping the standalone LinearMap and going straight to the categorical hom works.\n- **map_smul' across compHom-vs-restrictScalars actions**: `change` the goal to the native-action form `(\u0393SpecIso R).inv.hom r \u2022 f x`, then `rw [\u2190 hact]; exact h1` where `hact : appLE V \u22a4 e = (\u0393SpecIso R).inv` (proved by `rw [Scheme.Hom.appLE, fromSpec_app_self, Category.assoc, \u2190 Functor.map_comp, \u2190 op_comp, Subsingleton.elim _ (\ud835\udfd9 \u22a4), op_id, map_id, comp_id]`).\n- **IsIso of `tilde.map b'` for a `let`-bound b'**: `haveI : IsIso (tilde.map b') := by rw [show tilde.map b' = (tilde.functor _).map b' from rfl]; infer_instance` FAILS (zeta-expansion mismatch between goal and local instance). Use `inferInstanceAs (IsIso ((tilde.functor _).map b'))` \u2014 works even without `clear_value`.\n- **Unit-component bijectivity at open immersions**: `Adjunction.unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app (restrictAdjunction j) (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction j) N` + `restrictAdjunction_unit_app_app` (plain presheaf restriction along `j''\u1d41j\u207b\u00b9\u1d41V = V`) + component of `restrictFunctorIsoPullback`. When `rw [\u2190 AddCommGrpCat.comp_apply]` fails with \"target not type-correct under instances transparency\" (`\u0393((\ud835\udfed X.Modules).obj N, V)` forms), do `change`-restatement at the type-correct form, then close with `exact congrArg (fun \u03c6 => (AddCommGrpCat.Hom.hom \u03c6) y) hcomp` where `hcomp : f \u226b g = \ud835\udfd9 _` \u2014 both sides defeq, no rewriting in the wall.\n- **\u03a3-pair trace**: `tilde.toOpen_map_app` (naturality) + `toOpen_fromTilde\u0393_app` at `\u22a4` (+ `homOfLE le_top = \ud835\udfd9 \u22a4` by `Subsingleton.elim`) give `(tilde.map b' \u226b fromTilde\u0393).app \u22a4 \u2218 toOpen = b'` elementwise, via `congrArg`-chains only.",

      "body": "Recipe: building ModuleCat-R morphisms into sheaf-of-modules section objects (v4.31) \u2014 the ConcreteCategory.ofHom + presheaf-obj pattern, and the let-fvar IsIso gotcha\n\nLanded in `tildeIso_of_isQuasicoherent_isAffineOpen` (`QuotScheme.lean`, T12 run 0010). When you need `f : ModuleCat.of R M \u27f6 <sections object>` (e.g. to feed `tilde.map`):\n\n- **Target the honest `ModuleCat R` object** `(modulesSpecToSheaf.obj G).presheaf.obj (Opposite.op \u22a4)` \u2014 this is literally the domain module of Mathlib's `fromTilde\u0393`/`toOpen`. Do NOT target `moduleSpec\u0393Functor.obj G` via `ModuleCat.ofHom`/`\u2192\u2097` type ascriptions: elaboration whnf-unfolds the carrier past `restrictScalars`, and `Module R <unfolded carrier>` synthesis then fails (no refold; a letI at the folded form does not match either).\n- **Construct via `ConcreteCategory.ofHom { toFun := ..., map_add' := ..., map_smul' := ... }`** with the expected hom type ascribed \u2014 the instances come from the objects via the `(\u00b7 \u2192\u2097[R] \u00b7)` FC family, no synthesis. A bare `let blin : M \u2192\u2097[R] <object> := ...` fails; skipping the standalone LinearMap and going straight to the categorical hom works.\n- **map_smul' across compHom-vs-restrictScalars actions**: `change` the goal to the native-action form `(\u0393SpecIso R).inv.hom r \u2022 f x`, then `rw [\u2190 hact]; exact h1` where `hact : appLE V \u22a4 e = (\u0393SpecIso R).inv` (proved by `rw [Scheme.Hom.appLE, fromSpec_app_self, Category.assoc, \u2190 Functor.map_comp, \u2190 op_comp, Subsingleton.elim _ (\ud835\udfd9 \u22a4), op_id, map_id, comp_id]`).\n- **IsIso of `tilde.map b'` for a `let`-bound b'**: `haveI : IsIso (tilde.map b') := by rw [show tilde.map b' = (tilde.functor _).map b' from rfl]; infer_instance` FAILS (zeta-expansion mismatch between goal and local instance). Use `inferInstanceAs (IsIso ((tilde.functor _).map b'))` \u2014 works even without `clear_value`.\n- **Unit-component bijectivity at open immersions**: `Adjunction.unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app (restrictAdjunction j) (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction j) N` + `restrictAdjunction_unit_app_app` (plain presheaf restriction along `j''\u1d41j\u207b\u00b9\u1d41V = V`) + component of `restrictFunctorIsoPullback`. When `rw [\u2190 AddCommGrpCat.comp_apply]` fails with \"target not type-correct under instances transparency\" (`\u0393((\ud835\udfed X.Modules).obj N, V)` forms), do `change`-restatement at the type-correct form, then close with `exact congrArg (fun \u03c6 => (AddCommGrpCat.Hom.hom \u03c6) y) hcomp` where `hcomp : f \u226b g = \ud835\udfd9 _` \u2014 both sides defeq, no rewriting in the wall.\n- **\u03a3-pair trace**: `tilde.toOpen_map_app` (naturality) + `toOpen_fromTilde\u0393_app` at `\u22a4` (+ `homOfLE le_top = \ud835\udfd9 \u22a4` by `Subsingleton.elim`) give `(tilde.map b' \u226b fromTilde\u0393).app \u22a4 \u2218 toOpen = b'` elementwise, via `congrArg`-chains only.",

     8	/-!
     9	# Contractibility of the concrete section Čech complex
    10	
    11	This file proves the augmentation-degree contracting identity and packages all degreewise
    12	identities into a contracting homotopy.
    13	-/
    14	
    15	universe u
    16	
    17	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
    18	
    19	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    20	
    21	open Scheme.Modules
    22	
    23	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
    24	
    25	section ContractingHomotopy
    26	
    27	variable (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) [Finite 𝒰.I₀] (F : X.Modules) (V : TopologicalSpace.Opens X)
    28	variable (i_fix : 𝒰.I₀) (hiV : V ≤ coverOpen 𝒰 i_fix)
    29	
    30	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
    31	set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
    32	-- The augmentation-node identity expands two dependent product coordinates and their sums.
    33	set_option maxRecDepth 4000 in
    34	/-- **(I1)** The augmentation-node contracting identity:
    35	`𝟙 = π_{i_fix} ≫ ε + d⁰ ≫ h₁` on `Č⁰`. -/
    36	private lemma cechSection_comm_one :
    37	    𝟙 ((cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).X 1) =
    38	      cechSectionHomotopyZero 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV ≫ (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d 0 1 +
    39	        (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d 1 2 ≫ cechSectionHomotopyComp 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV 0 := by
    40	  ext t
    41	  apply (sectionCechProductAddEquiv (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)
    42	    ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0).injective
    43	  funext σ
    44	  refine Eq.symm ?_
    45	  have hsplit : ConcreteCategory.hom
    46	      (cechSectionHomotopyZero 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV ≫ (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d 0 1 +
    47	        (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d 1 2 ≫ cechSectionHomotopyComp 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV 0) t
    48	      = ConcreteCategory.hom (cechSectionHomotopyZero 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV ≫
    49	          (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d 0 1) t +
    50	        ConcreteCategory.hom ((cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d 1 2 ≫
    51	          cechSectionHomotopyComp 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV 0) t := by
    52	    rw [AddCommGrpCat.hom_add_apply]
    53	  refine Eq.trans (congrArg (fun y => sectionCechProductAddEquiv
    54	    (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V) ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0 y σ)
    55	    hsplit) ?_
    56	  refine Eq.trans (congrArg (fun y => y σ)
    57	    (map_add (sectionCechProductAddEquiv (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)
    58	      ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0) _ _)) ?_
    59	  -- piece 1: `π_{i_fix} ≫ ε` is `depDiff (depHomotopy t̃)` at the bottom level
    60	  have hpiece1 : sectionCechProductEquiv (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)
    61	      ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0
    62	      (ConcreteCategory.hom (cechSectionHomotopyZero 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV ≫
    63	        (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d 0 1) t) σ
    64	      = CombinatorialCech.depDiff (A := cechSectionCoeff 𝒰 F V) (cechSectionCoface 𝒰 F V)
    65	          (CombinatorialCech.depHomotopy i_fix (cechSectionPrepend 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV)
    66	            (fun τ => sectionCechProductEquiv (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)
    67	              ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0 t τ)) σ := by
    68	    refine Eq.trans (sectionCechProductEquiv_apply (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)
    69	      ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0 _ σ) ?_
    70	    refine Eq.trans (ConcreteCategory.comp_apply _ (Pi.π _ σ) _).symm ?_
    71	    refine Eq.trans (ConcreteCategory.congr_hom (Category.assoc
    72	      (cechSectionHomotopyZero 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV)
    73	      ((cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d 0 1) (Pi.π _ σ)) t) ?_
    74	    refine Eq.trans (ConcreteCategory.comp_apply _ _ t) ?_
    75	    refine Eq.trans (ConcreteCategory.congr_hom (sectionCechAugV_π 𝒰 F V σ)
    76	      (ConcreteCategory.hom (cechSectionHomotopyZero 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV) t)) ?_
    77	    refine Eq.symm ?_
    78	    refine Eq.trans (cechSectionDepDiff_zero 𝒰 F V _ σ) ?_
    79	    have htuple : ∀ ρ : Fin 0 → 𝒰.I₀,
    80	        cechSectionPrepend 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV 0 ρ
    81	          (sectionCechProductEquiv (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)
    82	            ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0 t (Fin.cons i_fix ρ))
    83	        = cechSectionPrepend 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV 0 Fin.elim0
    84	            (sectionCechProductEquiv (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)
    85	              ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0 t
    86	              (Fin.cons i_fix Fin.elim0)) := by
    87	      intro ρ
    88	      have hρ : ρ = Fin.elim0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
    89	      subst hρ
    90	      rfl
    91	    refine Eq.trans (DFunLike.congr_arg (cechSectionCoface 𝒰 F V 0 σ 0)
    92	      (htuple (σ ∘ (0 : Fin 1).succAbove))) ?_
    93	    refine DFunLike.congr_arg (cechSectionCoface 𝒰 F V 0 σ 0) ?_
    94	    refine DFunLike.congr_arg (cechSectionPrepend 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV 0 Fin.elim0) ?_
    95	    exact (sectionCechProductEquiv_apply (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)
    96	      ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0 t (Fin.cons i_fix Fin.elim0))
    97	  -- piece 2: `d⁰ ≫ h₁` is `depHomotopy (depDiff t̃)`
    98	  have hpiece2 : sectionCechProductEquiv (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)
    99	      ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0
   100	      (ConcreteCategory.hom ((cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d 1 2 ≫
   101	        cechSectionHomotopyComp 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV 0) t) σ
   102	      = CombinatorialCech.depHomotopy i_fix (cechSectionPrepend 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV)
   103	          (CombinatorialCech.depDiff (A := cechSectionCoeff 𝒰 F V) (cechSectionCoface 𝒰 F V)
   104	            (fun τ => sectionCechProductEquiv (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)
   105	              ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0 t τ)) σ := by
   106	    refine Eq.trans (congrArg (fun y => sectionCechProductEquiv (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)
   107	      ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0 y σ)
   108	      (ConcreteCategory.comp_apply _ _ t)) ?_
   109	    refine Eq.trans (cechSectionHomotopyComp_coord 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV 0 _ σ) ?_
   110	    exact DFunLike.congr_arg (cechSectionPrepend 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV 1 σ)
   111	      (cechSectionD_coord 𝒰 F V 0 t (Fin.cons i_fix σ))
   112	  refine Eq.trans (congrArg₂ (· + ·) hpiece1 hpiece2) ?_
   113	  refine Eq.trans (CombinatorialCech.depHomotopy_spec i_fix (cechSectionCoface 𝒰 F V)
   114	    (cechSectionPrepend 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV)
   115	    (fun {m} σ' y => cechSection_hu 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV σ' y)
   116	    (fun {m} σ' k y => cechSection_hsh 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV σ' k y)
   117	    (fun τ => sectionCechProductEquiv (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)
   118	      ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0 t τ) σ) ?_
   119	  exact congrArg (fun y => sectionCechProductEquiv (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)
   120	    ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0 y σ)
   121	    (ConcreteCategory.id_apply t).symm
   122	
   123	/-- The coinductive step: given the previous homotopy condition, the corrected component
   124	`h_{n+2} ≫ (𝟙 - p₂₁ ≫ d)` satisfies the next one (pure preadditive algebra from `(In)`
   125	and `d ∘ d = 0`). -/
   126	private lemma cechSection_succ_step (n : ℕ)
   127	    {f : (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).X (n + 1) ⟶ (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).X n}
   128	    {g : (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).X (n + 2) ⟶ (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).X (n + 1)}
   129	    (hp : 𝟙 ((cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).X (n + 1)) =
   130	      f ≫ (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d n (n + 1) +
   131	        (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d (n + 1) (n + 2) ≫ g) :
   132	    𝟙 ((cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).X (n + 2)) =
   133	      g ≫ (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d (n + 1) (n + 2) +
   134	        (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d (n + 2) (n + 3) ≫
   135	          (cechSectionHomotopyComp 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV (n + 1) ≫
   136	            (𝟙 ((cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).X (n + 2)) -
   137	              g ≫ (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d (n + 1) (n + 2))) := by
   138	  have hIn := cechSection_comm_succ 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV n
   139	  have hsub : (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d (n + 1) (n + 2) =
   140	      (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d (n + 1) (n + 2) ≫ g ≫
   141	        (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d (n + 1) (n + 2) := by
   142	    have h₀ := congrArg (fun m => m ≫ (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d (n + 1) (n + 2)) hp
   143	    simpa only [Category.id_comp, Preadditive.add_comp, Category.assoc,
   144	      HomologicalComplex.d_comp_d, comp_zero, zero_add] using h₀
   145	  have hd1E : (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d (n + 1) (n + 2) ≫
   146	      (𝟙 ((cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).X (n + 2)) -
   147	        g ≫ (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d (n + 1) (n + 2)) = 0 := by
   148	    rw [Preadditive.comp_sub, Category.comp_id, sub_eq_zero]
   149	    exact hsub
   150	  have hdb := eq_sub_iff_add_eq.mpr ((add_comm _ _).trans hIn.symm)
   151	  rw [← Category.assoc ((cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d (n + 2) (n + 3))
   152	    (cechSectionHomotopyComp 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV (n + 1)) _, hdb, Preadditive.sub_comp,
   153	    Category.id_comp, Category.assoc, hd1E, comp_zero, sub_zero]
   154	  abel
   155	
   156	end ContractingHomotopy
   157	
   158	set_option maxRecDepth 8000 in
   159	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
   160	set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
   161	-- Coinductive homotopy packaging has deeply nested dependent degree equalities.
   162	/-- The concrete augmented section Čech complex is contractible after choosing a cover member
   163	that contains `V`. -/
   164	noncomputable def cechSection_contractible (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) [Finite 𝒰.I₀]
   165	    (F : X.Modules) (V : TopologicalSpace.Opens X)
   166	    (i_fix : 𝒰.I₀) (hiV : V ≤ coverOpen 𝒰 i_fix) :
   167	    Homotopy (𝟙 ((sectionCechComplexV 𝒰 F V).augment (sectionCechAugV 𝒰 F V)
   168	      (sectionCechAugV_comp_d 𝒰 F V))) 0 :=
   169	  -- The prepend-`i_fix` contracting homotopy on the augmented concrete section complex,
   170	  -- assembled by `Homotopy.mkCoinductive` from the explicit components (`π_{i_fix}` at the
   171	  -- augmentation node, prepend-`i_fix` in the Čech degrees) and the three contracting
   172	  -- identities (I0)/(I1)/(In) proved above via the dependent combinatorial engine.
   173	  Homotopy.mkCoinductive _
   174	    (cechSectionHomotopyZero 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV)
   175	    ((HomologicalComplex.id_f _ _).trans (cechSection_comm_zero 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV))
   176	    (cechSectionHomotopyComp 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV 0)
   177	    ((HomologicalComplex.id_f _ _).trans (cechSection_comm_one 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV))
   178	    (fun n p =>
   179	      ⟨cechSectionHomotopyComp 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV (n + 1) ≫
   180	          (𝟙 (((sectionCechComplexV 𝒰 F V).augment (sectionCechAugV 𝒰 F V)
   181	              (sectionCechAugV_comp_d 𝒰 F V)).X (n + 2)) -
   182	            p.2.1 ≫ ((sectionCechComplexV 𝒰 F V).augment (sectionCechAugV 𝒰 F V)
   183	              (sectionCechAugV_comp_d 𝒰 F V)).d (n + 1) (n + 2)), by
   184	        have hp := (HomologicalComplex.id_f _ _).symm.trans p.2.2
   185	        exact (HomologicalComplex.id_f _ _).trans
   186	          (cechSection_succ_step 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV n hp)⟩)
   187	
   188	end AlgebraicGeometry

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.CechSectionIdentification

     8	/-!
     9	# Components of the concrete section Čech contraction
    10	
    11	This file constructs the restriction maps and homotopy components for the augmented concrete
    12	section Čech complex, together with the degree-zero contracting identity.
    13	-/
    14	
    15	universe u
    16	
    17	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
    18	
    19	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    20	
    21	open Scheme.Modules
    22	
    23	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
    24	
    25	/-! ### Additive product coordinates -/
    26	
    27	/-- The additive form of the dependent product coordinates used by the concrete section Čech
    28	complex.  Keeping the product equivalence bundled avoids repeating its additivity proof at each
    29	coordinatewise contracting identity. -/
    30	noncomputable def sectionCechProductAddEquiv {ι : Type u}
    31	    (U : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens X) (F : X.PresheafOfModules) (p : ℕ) :
    32	    ToType ((sectionCechCosimplicial U F).obj (SimplexCategory.mk p)) ≃+
    33	      (∀ σ : Fin (p + 1) → ι,
    34	        ToType (F.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op (⨅ k, U (σ k))))) where
    35	  toFun := sectionCechProductEquiv U F p
    36	  invFun := (sectionCechProductEquiv U F p).symm
    37	  left_inv := (sectionCechProductEquiv U F p).left_inv
    38	  right_inv := (sectionCechProductEquiv U F p).right_inv
    39	  map_add' x y := by
    40	    funext σ
    41	    calc
    42	      sectionCechProductEquiv U F p (x + y) σ =
    43	          ConcreteCategory.hom
    44	            (Pi.π (fun σ : Fin (p + 1) → ι =>
    45	              F.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op (⨅ k, U (σ k)))) σ) (x + y) :=
    46	        sectionCechProductEquiv_apply U F p (x + y) σ
    47	      _ = ConcreteCategory.hom
    48	            (Pi.π (fun σ : Fin (p + 1) → ι =>
    49	              F.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op (⨅ k, U (σ k)))) σ) x +
    50	          ConcreteCategory.hom
    51	            (Pi.π (fun σ : Fin (p + 1) → ι =>
    52	              F.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op (⨅ k, U (σ k)))) σ) y := by
    53	        exact map_add _ x y
    54	      _ = sectionCechProductEquiv U F p x σ +
    55	          sectionCechProductEquiv U F p y σ := by
    56	        rw [sectionCechProductEquiv_apply, sectionCechProductEquiv_apply]
    57	
    58	/-! ## Contracting homotopy on the augmented concrete section Čech complex -/
    59	
    60	/-! ### Restriction engine
    61	
    62	The dependent-coefficient combinatorial Čech engine (`CombinatorialCech.depHomotopy_spec`,
    63	CechAcyclic.lean) is instantiated with the augmentation node `Γ(V, F)` as level `0` and the
    64	restricted Čech coefficients `Γ(⨅ₖ (U_{σ k} ⊓ V), F)` as levels `≥ 1`.  The coface maps `δ`
    65	are the presheaf face restrictions (level `0 → 1` is the augmentation restriction), and the
    66	prepend maps `c` are genuine restrictions because `V ≤ coverOpen 𝒰 i_fix` forces
    67	`U'_{i_fix·σ} = U'_σ`.  The `hu`/`hsh` compatibilities collapse to "two parallel restriction
    68	chains between the same opens agree". -/
    69	
    70	section RestrictionEngine
    71	
    72	variable (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) (F : X.Modules) (V : TopologicalSpace.Opens X)
    73	
    74	/-- Composite of two presheaf restrictions is the direct restriction (local copy of the
    75	`CechBridge` private helper `restr_trans`). -/
    76	private lemma restriction_comp_apply (P : (TopologicalSpace.Opens ↥X)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Ab.{u})
    77	    {A B C : TopologicalSpace.Opens ↥X} (h1 : A ≤ B) (h2 : B ≤ C)
    78	    (x : ToType (P.obj (Opposite.op C))) :
    79	    ConcreteCategory.hom (P.map (homOfLE h1).op)
    80	        (ConcreteCategory.hom (P.map (homOfLE h2).op) x)
    81	      = ConcreteCategory.hom (P.map (homOfLE (h1.trans h2)).op) x := by
    82	  rw [← ConcreteCategory.comp_apply, ← P.map_comp, ← op_comp]
    83	  rfl
    84	
    85	/-- Two parallel presheaf restrictions agree (poset-hom uniqueness; local copy of the
    86	`CechBridge` private helper `restr_op_unique`). -/
    87	private lemma restriction_eq_of_parallel (P : (TopologicalSpace.Opens ↥X)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Ab.{u})
    88	    {A C : TopologicalSpace.Opens ↥X} (f g : Opposite.op C ⟶ Opposite.op A)

    90	    ConcreteCategory.hom (P.map f) x = ConcreteCategory.hom (P.map g) x := by

    93	/-- A nonempty restricted Čech intersection is contained in `V`. -/
    94	private lemma restrictedIntersection_le {m : ℕ} (σ : Fin (m + 1) → 𝒰.I₀) :
    95	    (⨅ k, (coverOpen 𝒰 (σ k) ⊓ V)) ≤ V :=
    96	  le_trans (iInf_le _ 0) inf_le_right

    98	/-- Prepending `i_fix` does not shrink the restricted intersection (positive levels). -/
    99	private lemma restrictedIntersection_le_cons {m : ℕ} (i_fix : 𝒰.I₀) (hiV : V ≤ coverOpen 𝒰 i_fix)
   100	    (σ : Fin (m + 1) → 𝒰.I₀) :
   101	    (⨅ k, (coverOpen 𝒰 (σ k) ⊓ V)) ≤
   102	      ⨅ k, (coverOpen 𝒰 ((Fin.cons i_fix σ : Fin (m + 2) → 𝒰.I₀) k) ⊓ V) := by
   103	  refine le_iInf fun k => ?_
   104	  refine Fin.cases ?_ ?_ k
   105	  · rw [Fin.cons_zero]
   106	    exact le_trans (restrictedIntersection_le 𝒰 V σ) (le_inf hiV le_rfl)
   107	  · intro j
   108	    rw [Fin.cons_succ]
   109	    exact iInf_le _ j

   111	/-- Prepending `i_fix` to the empty tuple yields an intersection containing `V`
   112	(the augmentation node case). -/
   113	private lemma le_restrictedIntersection_cons_empty (i_fix : 𝒰.I₀) (hiV : V ≤ coverOpen 𝒰 i_fix)

   115	    V ≤ ⨅ k, (coverOpen 𝒰 ((Fin.cons i_fix σ : Fin 1 → 𝒰.I₀) k) ⊓ V) := by
   116	  refine le_iInf fun k => ?_
   117	  rw [Fin.fin_one_eq_zero k, Fin.cons_zero]

   120	/-- The open underlying the level-`m` contracting-homotopy coefficient: level `0` is `V` (the
   121	augmentation node), level `m+1` is the restricted intersection `⨅ₖ (U_{σ k} ⊓ V)`. -/
   122	private def homotopyOpen : (m : ℕ) → (Fin m → 𝒰.I₀) → TopologicalSpace.Opens ↥X
   123	  | 0, _ => V
   124	  | _ + 1, σ => ⨅ k, (coverOpen 𝒰 (σ k) ⊓ V)

   126	/-- The coface inclusion of the contracting-homotopy opens. -/
   127	private lemma homotopyOpen_le_coface : ∀ {m : ℕ} (σ : Fin (m + 1) → 𝒰.I₀) (j : Fin (m + 1)),
   128	    homotopyOpen 𝒰 V (m + 1) σ ≤ homotopyOpen 𝒰 V m (σ ∘ j.succAbove)
   129	  | 0, σ, _ => restrictedIntersection_le 𝒰 V σ
   130	  | _ + 1, _, j => le_iInf fun l => iInf_le _ (j.succAbove l)

   132	/-- The prepend inclusion of the contracting-homotopy opens (prepending `i_fix` does not shrink the
   133	open, because `V ≤ coverOpen 𝒰 i_fix`). -/
   134	private lemma homotopyOpen_le_prepend (i_fix : 𝒰.I₀) (hiV : V ≤ coverOpen 𝒰 i_fix) :
   135	    ∀ {m : ℕ} (σ : Fin m → 𝒰.I₀),
   136	      homotopyOpen 𝒰 V m σ ≤ homotopyOpen 𝒰 V (m + 1) (Fin.cons i_fix σ)
   137	  | 0, σ => le_restrictedIntersection_cons_empty 𝒰 V i_fix hiV σ
   138	  | _ + 1, σ => restrictedIntersection_le_cons 𝒰 V i_fix hiV σ

   140	/-- Dependent coefficient family for the contracting-homotopy engine: the sections of `F` over
   141	`homotopyOpen m σ`.  Kept as a reducible abbreviation so the `AddCommGroup` instance is the
   142	generic one on `Ab`-objects (no bespoke match-instance). -/
   143	noncomputable abbrev cechSectionCoeff (m : ℕ) (σ : Fin m → 𝒰.I₀) : Type u :=
   144	  ToType (((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F).presheaf.obj
   145	    (Opposite.op (homotopyOpen 𝒰 V m σ)))

   147	/-- The engine coface maps: presheaf face restrictions (level `0 → 1` is the augmentation
   148	restriction `Γ(V) → Γ(U'_σ)`). -/
   149	noncomputable def cechSectionCoface (m : ℕ) (σ : Fin (m + 1) → 𝒰.I₀)
   150	    (j : Fin (m + 1)) :
   151	    cechSectionCoeff 𝒰 F V m (σ ∘ j.succAbove) →+ cechSectionCoeff 𝒰 F V (m + 1) σ :=
   152	  ConcreteCategory.hom (((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F).presheaf.map
   153	    (homOfLE (homotopyOpen_le_coface 𝒰 V σ j)).op)
   154	
   155	/-- The engine prepend maps: genuine restrictions (level `1 → 0` is the restriction
   156	`Γ(U'_{(i_fix)}) → Γ(V)` along `V ≤ U'_{i_fix}`). -/
   157	noncomputable def cechSectionPrepend (i_fix : 𝒰.I₀)
   158	    (hiV : V ≤ coverOpen 𝒰 i_fix) (m : ℕ) (σ : Fin m → 𝒰.I₀) :
   159	    cechSectionCoeff 𝒰 F V (m + 1) (Fin.cons i_fix σ) →+ cechSectionCoeff 𝒰 F V m σ :=
   160	  ConcreteCategory.hom (((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F).presheaf.map
   161	    (homOfLE (homotopyOpen_le_prepend 𝒰 V i_fix hiV σ)).op)
   162	
   163	/-- Transport of a Čech coefficient along an equality of index tuples is the canonical
   164	restriction between the (equal) intersection opens. -/
   165	private lemma cechSectionCoeff_transport {m : ℕ} {τ₁ τ₂ : Fin (m + 1) → 𝒰.I₀}
   166	    (h : τ₁ = τ₂)
   167	    (hle : homotopyOpen 𝒰 V (m + 1) τ₂ ≤ homotopyOpen 𝒰 V (m + 1) τ₁)
   168	    (y : cechSectionCoeff 𝒰 F V (m + 1) τ₁) :
   169	    (h ▸ y : cechSectionCoeff 𝒰 F V (m + 1) τ₂)
   170	      = ConcreteCategory.hom
   171	          (((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F).presheaf.map (homOfLE hle).op)
   172	          y := by
   173	  subst h
   174	  rw [show homOfLE hle = 𝟙 _ from Subsingleton.elim _ _, op_id,
   175	    CategoryTheory.Functor.map_id]
   176	  rfl
   177	
   178	/-- Unit compatibility `hu` for the contracting-homotopy engine: deleting the prepended
   179	`i_fix` and then applying the prepend restriction is the identity transport (both sides are
   180	restriction chains between the same opens). -/
   181	lemma cechSection_hu (i_fix : 𝒰.I₀) (hiV : V ≤ coverOpen 𝒰 i_fix)
   182	    {m : ℕ} (σ : Fin (m + 1) → 𝒰.I₀)
   183	    (y : cechSectionCoeff 𝒰 F V (m + 1)
   184	      ((Fin.cons i_fix σ : Fin (m + 2) → 𝒰.I₀) ∘ (0 : Fin (m + 2)).succAbove)) :
   185	    cechSectionPrepend 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV (m + 1) σ
   186	        (cechSectionCoface 𝒰 F V (m + 1) (Fin.cons i_fix σ) 0 y)
   187	      = (CombinatorialCech.cons_comp_zero_succAbove i_fix σ) ▸ y := by
   188	  rw [cechSectionCoeff_transport 𝒰 F V (CombinatorialCech.cons_comp_zero_succAbove i_fix σ)
   189	    (le_of_eq (by rw [CombinatorialCech.cons_comp_zero_succAbove i_fix σ]))]
   190	  exact (restriction_comp_apply _ _ _ y).trans (restriction_eq_of_parallel _ _ _ y)
   191	
   192	/-- Shift compatibility `hsh` for the contracting-homotopy engine: prepend commutes with the later
   193	cofaces (both sides are restriction chains between the same opens). -/
   194	lemma cechSection_hsh (i_fix : 𝒰.I₀) (hiV : V ≤ coverOpen 𝒰 i_fix)
   195	    {m : ℕ} (σ : Fin (m + 1) → 𝒰.I₀) (k : Fin (m + 1))
   196	    (y : cechSectionCoeff 𝒰 F V (m + 1)
   197	      ((Fin.cons i_fix σ : Fin (m + 2) → 𝒰.I₀) ∘ (k.succ).succAbove)) :
   198	    cechSectionPrepend 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV (m + 1) σ
   199	        (cechSectionCoface 𝒰 F V (m + 1) (Fin.cons i_fix σ) k.succ y)
   200	      = cechSectionCoface 𝒰 F V m σ k
   201	          (cechSectionPrepend 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV m (σ ∘ k.succAbove)
   202	            ((CombinatorialCech.cons_comp_succAbove_succ i_fix σ k) ▸ y)) := by
   203	  have hle : homotopyOpen 𝒰 V (m + 1) (Fin.cons i_fix (σ ∘ k.succAbove)) ≤
   204	      homotopyOpen 𝒰 V (m + 1) ((Fin.cons i_fix σ : Fin (m + 2) → 𝒰.I₀) ∘ (k.succ).succAbove) :=
   205	    le_of_eq (by rw [CombinatorialCech.cons_comp_succAbove_succ i_fix σ k])
   206	  rw [cechSectionCoeff_transport 𝒰 F V
   207	    (CombinatorialCech.cons_comp_succAbove_succ i_fix σ k) hle]
   208	  refine Eq.trans (restriction_comp_apply _ (homotopyOpen_le_prepend 𝒰 V i_fix hiV σ)
   209	    (homotopyOpen_le_coface 𝒰 V (Fin.cons i_fix σ) k.succ) y) ?_
   210	  refine Eq.trans (restriction_eq_of_parallel _ _ (homOfLE ((homotopyOpen_le_coface 𝒰 V σ k).trans
   211	    ((homotopyOpen_le_prepend 𝒰 V i_fix hiV (σ ∘ k.succAbove)).trans hle))).op y) ?_
   212	  refine Eq.symm ?_
   213	  refine Eq.trans (DFunLike.congr_arg (cechSectionCoface 𝒰 F V m σ k)
   214	    (restriction_comp_apply _ (homotopyOpen_le_prepend 𝒰 V i_fix hiV (σ ∘ k.succAbove)) hle y)) ?_
   215	  exact restriction_comp_apply _ (homotopyOpen_le_coface 𝒰 V σ k)
   216	    ((homotopyOpen_le_prepend 𝒰 V i_fix hiV (σ ∘ k.succAbove)).trans hle) y
   217

   220	/-! ### Degree-0 augmentation seam — helper bricks for `sectionCechAugV_π`.
   221	
   222	The seam unwinds `sectionCechAugV ≫ Pi.π σ` through the proved Base seams.  The Čech
   223	augmentation composed with the push–pull of *any* `Over X`-morphism `g : Y ⟶ Y₀` into the
   224	backbone collapses — through the terminal object `Over.mk (𝟙 X)` of `Over X` — to the
   225	pullback–pushforward adjunction unit at `Y.hom` (`cechAugmentation_pushPullMap`); the unit, in
   226	turn, reads through the per-leg section identification `pushPull_leg_sections` as the plain
   227	presheaf restriction (`unit_pushPull_leg_sections`), because it is conjugate via
   228	`Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq` to the restriction adjunction whose unit *is* the restriction on
   229	sections (`Scheme.Modules.restrictAdjunction_unit_app_app`). -/
   230	
   231	section AugSeam
   232	
   233	/-- An `eqToHom` between section groups of an abelian presheaf over (propositionally) equal
   234	opens is the presheaf restriction along the induced inclusion.  Transport-killer for the
   235	augmentation seam. -/
   236	private lemma eqToHom_eq_restriction (P : (TopologicalSpace.Opens ↥X)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Ab.{u})
   237	    {A B : TopologicalSpace.Opens ↥X} (hAB : A = B) (hle : B ≤ A)
   238	    (h : P.obj (Opposite.op A) = P.obj (Opposite.op B)) :
   239	    eqToHom h = P.map (homOfLE hle).op := by
   240	  subst hAB
   241	  refine Eq.trans (eqToHom_refl _ h) ?_
   242	  refine Eq.trans (P.map_id (Opposite.op A)).symm ?_
   243	  exact congrArg P.map (congrArg Quiver.Hom.op (Subsingleton.elim (𝟙 A) (homOfLE hle)))
   244	
   245	/-- Precomposing the scheme-level push–pull comparison `rawPushPullMap` with the
   246	pullback–pushforward adjunction unit at the source structure map yields the unit at the
   247	target structure map (`η^{p₁} ≫ G(a) = η^{p₂}`, the mate-calculus collapse of the degree-`0`
   248	augmentation leg). -/
   249	private lemma rawPushPullMap_unit {Z₁ Z₂ : Scheme.{u}} (a : Z₂ ⟶ Z₁)
   250	    (p₁ : Z₁ ⟶ X) (p₂ : Z₂ ⟶ X) (w : a ≫ p₁ = p₂) (F : X.Modules) :
   251	    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction p₁).unit.app F ≫
   252	        rawPushPullMap a p₁ p₂ w F =
   253	      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction p₂).unit.app F := by
   254	  subst w
   255	  rw [rawPushPullMap_self, pushPull_unit_comp a p₁ F]
   256	  refine congrArg (fun m =>
   257	    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction p₁).unit.app F ≫ m) ?_
   258	  refine Eq.trans ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward p₁).map_comp _ _) ?_
   259	  refine congrArg (fun m => (Scheme.Modules.pushforward p₁).map
   260	    ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction a).unit.app
   261	      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback p₁).obj F)) ≫ m) ?_
   262	  -- `pushforward` is strict: `p₁_*(a_* χ) = (pushforwardComp).hom ≫ (a ≫ p₁)_* χ`
   263	  -- (the comparison cell is the identity on sections).
   264	  apply Scheme.Modules.hom_ext
   265	  intro U
   266	  rfl
   267	
   268	/-- The inverse of the Čech-nerve point identification is the pullback–pushforward
   269	adjunction unit of the identity morphism. -/
   270	private lemma cechNervePointIso_inv_eq_unit (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) (F : X.Modules) :
   271	    (cechNervePointIso 𝒰 F).inv =
   272	      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction (𝟙 X)).unit.app F := by
   273	  have star := unit_conjugateEquiv (Adjunction.id (C := X.Modules))
   274	    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction (𝟙 X)) (Scheme.Modules.pullbackId X).hom F
   275	  rw [Scheme.Modules.conjugateEquiv_pullbackId_hom] at star
   276	  simp only [Adjunction.id_unit, NatTrans.id_app, Functor.id_obj] at star
   277	  have star2 : (Scheme.Modules.pushforwardId X).inv.app F =
   278	      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction (𝟙 X)).unit.app F ≫
   279	        (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (𝟙 X)).map ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackId X).hom.app F) :=
   280	    (Category.id_comp _).symm.trans star
   281	  have hnat := (Scheme.Modules.pushforwardId X).inv.naturality
   282	    ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackId X).inv.app F)
   283	  simp only [Functor.id_obj, Functor.id_map] at hnat
   284	  refine Eq.trans (hnat : (cechNervePointIso 𝒰 F).inv = _) ?_
   285	  refine Eq.trans (congrArg (fun m => m ≫ (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (𝟙 X)).map
   286	    ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackId X).inv.app F)) star2) ?_
   287	  refine Eq.trans (Category.assoc _ _ _) ?_
   288	  refine Eq.trans (congrArg (fun m =>
   289	    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction (𝟙 X)).unit.app F ≫ m)
   290	    (((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (𝟙 X)).map_comp _ _).symm)) ?_
   291	  refine Eq.trans (congrArg (fun m =>
   292	    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction (𝟙 X)).unit.app F ≫
   293	      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (𝟙 X)).map m) (Iso.hom_inv_id_app _ _)) ?_
   294	  exact (congrArg (fun m =>
   295	      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction (𝟙 X)).unit.app F ≫ m)
   296	      ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (𝟙 X)).map_id _)).trans (Category.comp_id _)
   297	
   298	/-- The Čech augmentation composed with the push–pull of *any* `Over X`-morphism into the
   299	degree-`0` backbone is the pullback–pushforward adjunction unit at the structure map: the
   300	composite `Y ⟶ Y₀ ⟶ Over.mk (𝟙 X)` is a morphism into the terminal object, so the
   301	augmentation leg needs no unwinding. -/
   302	private lemma cechAugmentation_pushPullMap (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) (F : X.Modules)
   303	    {Y : Over X}
   304	    (g : Y ⟶ (coverCechNerveOver 𝒰).obj (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk 0))) :
   305	    cechAugmentation 𝒰 F ≫ pushPullMap F g =
   306	      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction Y.hom).unit.app F := by
   307	  have happ : (CechNerve 𝒰 F).hom.app (SimplexCategory.mk 0) =
   308	      pushPullMap F
   309	        ((coverCechNerveOverAug 𝒰).hom.app (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk 0))) :=
   310	    Eq.trans rfl (Category.id_comp _)
   311	  rw [cechAugmentation, Category.assoc]
   312	  refine Eq.trans (congrArg (fun m => (cechNervePointIso 𝒰 F).inv ≫ m)
   313	    (Eq.trans (congrArg (fun m => m ≫ pushPullMap F g) happ)
   314	      ((pushPullMap_comp F _ g).symm))) ?_
   315	  rw [cechNervePointIso_inv_eq_unit, pushPullMap_eq_raw]
   316	  exact rawPushPullMap_unit _ _ _ _ F

   318	/-- The pullback–pushforward unit reads through the per-leg section identification as the
   319	plain `F`-restriction `Γ(V, F) → Γ(U_σ ∩ V, F)`. -/
   320	private lemma unit_pushPull_leg_sections (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) [Finite 𝒰.I₀] (F : X.Modules)
   321	    {p : ℕ} (σ : Fin (p + 1) → 𝒰.I₀) (V : TopologicalSpace.Opens X) :
   322	    (Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf X ⋙
   323	        (CategoryTheory.evaluation (TopologicalSpace.Opens X)ᵒᵖ (Ab.{u})).obj
   324	          (Opposite.op V)).map
   325	        ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
   326	          (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).unit.app F) ≫
   327	      (pushPull_leg_sections 𝒰 F σ V).hom =
   328	    ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F).presheaf.map
   329	      (homOfLE (inf_le_right : coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ ⊓ V ≤ V)).op := by
   330	  have hW : Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ) ''ᵁ
   331	        (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ) ⁻¹ᵁ V) = coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ ⊓ V := by
   332	    rw [Scheme.Hom.image_preimage_eq_opensRange_inf, Scheme.Opens.opensRange_ι]
   333	  -- (i) the leg iso, with its `eqToHom` transport canonicalised to the `congrArg` form
   334	  -- (definitional: projections of `Iso.trans`/`eqToIso` plus proof irrelevance)
   335	  have hdec : (pushPull_leg_sections 𝒰 F σ V).hom =
   336	      (Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf X ⋙
   337	          (CategoryTheory.evaluation (TopologicalSpace.Opens X)ᵒᵖ (Ab.{u})).obj
   338	            (Opposite.op V)).map
   339	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).map
   340	          ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctorIsoPullback
   341	            (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).inv.app F)) ≫
   342	      eqToHom (congrArg
   343	        (fun W => ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F).presheaf.obj (Opposite.op W))
   344	        hW) := rfl
   345	  -- (ii) the pullback unit is conjugate to the restriction unit via `leftAdjointUniq`
   346	  -- (`restrictFunctorIsoPullback` *is* the `leftAdjointUniq` iso, definitionally)
   347	  have hLAU : (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
   348	        (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).unit.app F ≫
   349	      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).map
   350	        ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctorIsoPullback
   351	          (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).inv.app F) =
   352	      (Scheme.Modules.restrictAdjunction
   353	        (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).unit.app F := by
   354	    have h0 : (Scheme.Modules.restrictAdjunction
   355	          (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).unit.app F ≫
   356	        (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).map
   357	          ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctorIsoPullback
   358	            (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).hom.app F) =
   359	        (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
   360	          (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).unit.app F :=
   361	      Adjunction.unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app _ _ F
   362	    refine Eq.trans (congrArg (fun m => m ≫
   363	      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).map
   364	        ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctorIsoPullback
   365	          (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).inv.app F)) h0.symm) ?_
   366	    refine Eq.trans (Category.assoc _ _ _) ?_
   367	    refine Eq.trans (congrArg (fun m => (Scheme.Modules.restrictAdjunction
   368	        (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).unit.app F ≫ m)
   369	      (((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).map_comp
   370	        _ _).symm)) ?_
   371	    refine Eq.trans (congrArg (fun m => (Scheme.Modules.restrictAdjunction
   372	        (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).unit.app F ≫
   373	        (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).map m)
   374	      (Iso.hom_inv_id_app _ _)) ?_
   375	    exact (congrArg (fun m => (Scheme.Modules.restrictAdjunction
   376	        (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).unit.app F ≫ m)
   377	      ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (Scheme.Opens.ι (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ))).map_id _)).trans
   378	      (Category.comp_id _)
   379	  -- (iii) the restriction unit on sections is the plain restriction (definitional,
   380	  -- `Scheme.Modules.restrictAdjunction_unit_app_app`)
   381	  have hunit : (Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf X ⋙
   382	        (CategoryTheory.evaluation (TopologicalSpace.Opens X)ᵒᵖ (Ab.{u})).obj
   383	          (Opposite.op V)).map

## §3 THE BALLOON — THE LOCALLY-CLOSED CARVING (obligation 3, DECIDED)

### 3.1 The decision

> **(D3) The two-window multiplication carve.** Inside the ported product
> `Gr := Gr(g, H_M) ×_{k'} Gr(g, H_{M+s})`, the divisor functor is the subfunctor cut
> by the SINGLE closed condition
>
> `(♦)  the composite  H_s ⊗_{k'} K ⟶ H_{M+s} ⊗ R ⟶ (H_{M+s} ⊗ R)/K′  vanishes`
>
> (`H_s ⊗ K → H_{M+s} ⊗ R` = the multiplication map `μ ⊗ R` restricted to `K`), i.e.
> `Div^g ≅ Z(♦) ⊆ Gr` as a CLOSED subscheme. There is **no open condition in the
> carve**: `Div^g` of a proper smooth curve is proper over `k'`, and the design realizes
> this literally. Locally-closed-ness of the parent's mandate is delivered as
> closed-in-`Gr` (a fortiori locally closed).

The condition `(♦)` is one vanishing-of-a-map condition between finite projective
modules — the **equalizer/closed-immersion gift shape**: over a chart ring `R` of `Gr`,
`{R → R' : (♦) ⊗ R' holds}` is represented by `Spec (R/I_♦)` with `I_♦` the entries
ideal (embed the target in a finite free module — projective — and take coordinate
entries on generators of `H_s ⊗ K`); the closed immersion is
`IsClosedImmersion.spec_of_surjective` (mathlib
`AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/ClosedImmersion.lean:99`, verified; the `Spec(R/I) → Spec R`
instance at `:113–115`). Globalization over the glued `Gr` by uniqueness of the
universal property on the frame atlas. The Over-form equalizer gift
`isClosedImmersion_equalizer_ι_left` (mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/Separated.lean:273`,
verified) is the categorical fallback spelling if the entries-ideal route fights;
DAT-C's canonical-section normalization consumes the same gift (parent §2.2.3b).

### 3.2 The fibrewise heart (P-fib) — statement, and honest status

> **(P-fib)** Over any field `K ⊇ k'` (standing pack via `BaseChangeInstances`), let
> `K_M ⊆ H_M ⊗ K`, `K' ⊆ H_{M+s} ⊗ K` be subspaces of codimension exactly `g` with
> `μ(H_s ⊗ K_M) ⊆ K'`. Then there is a UNIQUE effective divisor `D` with
> `deg K D = g`, `K_M = H⁰(𝒪(MF − D))`, and `K' = H⁰(𝒪((M+s)F − D))`.

⟸ is §2.3. ⟹ is THE mountain — this is the honest content behind the parent's
"colength bookkeeping" slogan, and it is a genuine persistence theorem (the
constant-Hilbert-polynomial/Gotzmann-number-`g` instance, curve-specialized). **Status:
proof route designed to lane level (§3.3); the endgame F3 was NOT closed in this
design pass.** The route below is curve-specific and uses only tree-native tools; no
step needs machinery the route banned. The staged-probe mandate (§5) makes F3 the
campaign's first deliverable, before any relative work is committed.

    Source: [Nitsure], §4, Theorem “generic flatness”. Let \(S\) be a noetherian integral scheme, \(p : X \to S\) a finite-type morphism, and \(\mathcal{F}\) a coherent \(\mathcal{O}_X\)-module. Then there exists a non-empty open subscheme \(U \subseteq S\) such that the restriction of \(\mathcal{F}\) to \(X_U = p^{-1}(U)\) is \(\mathcal{O}_U\)-flat.

    blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html:2124:

    Source: [Nitsure], §4, Theorem “flattening stratification”; cf. [Stacks Project], tag 052H. Let \(S\) be a noetherian scheme and \(\mathcal{F}\) a coherent sheaf on the relative projective space \(\mathbb {P}^n_S\) over \(S\). Then:

    blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html:2144:

    Following [Nitsure], §4, the construction reduces to the special case \(n = 0\), assembled over the relative twists \(\pi _* \mathcal{F}(N+i)\). As the argument is local on \(S\) (the strata glue by their universal property, part (ii)), and as the three conclusions are proved through the sub-lemmas below, we assemble them in the order (i), (ii), (iii).

    blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html:2194:

    Source: [Nitsure], §4 (special case \(n=0\) of the main theorem). Let \(S\) be a noetherian scheme and let \(\mathcal{F}\) be a coherent \(\mathcal{O}_S\)-module. For each integer \(e \ge 0\), there exists a locally-closed subscheme \(S_e \hookrightarrow S\) whose underlying set is \(\{ s \in S : \dim _{\kappa (s)} \mathcal{F}|_s = e\} \). The family \(\{ S_e\} _e\) is a finite, mutually disjoint, set-theoretically covering stratification of \(S\), and a morphism \(f : T \to S\) pulls back \(\mathcal{F}\) to a locally-free \(\mathcal{O}_T\)-module of rank \(e\) if and only if \(f\) factors through \(S_e\). The function \(s \mapsto \dim _{\kappa (s)} \mathcal{F}|_s\) is upper-semicontinuous on \(S\).

    blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html:2206:

    By [Nitsure], §4 (verbatim above): for \(s \in S\), Nakayama produces a neighbourhood \(V\) of \(s\) and a right-exact local presentation \(\mathcal{O}_V^{\oplus m} \xrightarrow {\psi } \mathcal{O}_V^{\oplus e} \to \mathcal{F}|_V \to 0\) where \(e = \dim _{\kappa (s)} \mathcal{F}|_s\). The closed subscheme \(V_e \hookrightarrow V\) defined by the ideal sheaf generated by the matrix entries of \(\psi \) represents the locus where \(\mathcal{F}\) becomes locally free of rank \(e\): by right-exactness of tensor product, a base change \(f : T \to V\) has \(f^* \mathcal{F}\) locally free of rank \(e\) iff \(f^* \psi = 0\), iff \(f\) factors through \(V_e\). Glueing the \(V_e\) over the cover of \(S\) by such neighbourhoods (and intersecting with \(V \setminus \bigcup _{e' {\gt} e} V_{e'}\) to get the strictly-equal-to-\(e\) stratum) produces the locally-closed \(S_e\). Upper-semicontinuity of \(e\) follows because the rank of \(\psi \) is lower-semicontinuous.

    blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html:2272:

    Source: [Nitsure], §4 (general case, reduction by Noetherian induction). Let \(S\) be a noetherian scheme, \(\pi : \mathbb {P}^n_S \to S\) the relative projective space, and \(\mathcal{F}\) a coherent sheaf on \(\mathbb {P}^n_S\). Then there exist finitely many reduced, locally-closed, pairwise disjoint subschemes \(V_i \hookrightarrow S\) whose set-theoretic union is \(|S|\) and such that \(\mathcal{F}|_{\mathbb {P}^n_{V_i}}\) is flat over \(\mathcal{O}_{V_i}\) for each \(i\). Consequently, only finitely many Hilbert polynomials \(P_s(m) = \chi (\mathbb {P}^n_s, \mathcal{F}_s(m))\) occur as \(s\) varies over \(S\).

    blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html:2284:

    By [Nitsure], §4: \(S\) being noetherian, decompose \(|S| = \bigcup Y_j\) into finitely many irreducible components, each closed. For an irreducible component \(Y\), let \(U \subseteq Y\) be the open subset not lying on any other component, given the reduced subscheme structure (an integral, locally-closed subscheme of \(S\)). By 582 applied to \(\mathcal{F}|_{\mathbb {P}^n_U}\), there is a non-empty open \(V \subseteq U\) over which \(\mathcal{F}\) is flat. Replace \(S\) by the reduced closed complement \(S \setminus V\) and repeat. Noetherianity of \(S\) terminates the induction in finitely many steps, producing the \(V_i\). On each \(V_i\) the Hilbert polynomial is locally constant (flat families have locally constant Hilbert polynomial), hence takes finitely many values on the noetherian (hence quasi-compact) scheme \(V_i\); the finite union of finite sets is finite.

    blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html:2354:

    Source: [Nitsure], §4 (assembly step combining the \(n=0\) special case applied to direct images \(\pi _*\mathcal{F}(N+i)\)). Let \(S\), \(\pi : \mathbb {P}^n_S \to S\), \(\mathcal{F}\) be as in 583. There exists an integer \(N \ge 0\) such that for every \(s \in S\) the higher cohomologies \(H^r(\mathbb {P}^n_s, \mathcal{F}_s(m))\) vanish for all \(r \ge 1\), \(m \ge N\), and the base-change homomorphism \((\pi _* \mathcal{F}(m))|_s \to H^0(\mathbb {P}^n_s, \mathcal{F}_s(m))\) is an isomorphism for \(m \ge N\), \(s \in S\). Iterating the \(n=0\) stratification (584) on the coherent sheaves \(E_i := \pi _* \mathcal{F}(N+i)\) for \(i = 0, \dots , n\) produces a finite collection of locally-closed subschemes \(W_{e_0, \dots , e_n} \subseteq S\) indexed by tuples \((e_0, \dots , e_n) \in \mathbb {Z}^{n+1}\). Re-indexing each tuple by the unique numerical polynomial \(f \in \mathbb {Q}[\lambda ]\) of degree \(\le n\) with \(f(N+i) = e_i\) gives a finite stratification \(\{ W_f\} \) of \(S\), and the locally-closed subschemes \(S_f \subseteq W_f\) of 583 are obtained by further intersecting with the closed-subscheme conditions that \(\pi _* \mathcal{F}(N+i)|_{W_f}\) be locally free of rank \(f(N+i)\) for all \(i \ge 0\) (terminating by Noetherianity).

    blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html:2366:

    By 585, the family of Hilbert polynomials \(\{ P_s\} \) on \(S\) is finite, and there is a finite stratification \(\{ V_i\} \) of \(S\) on each of which \(\mathcal{F}\) is flat with locally-constant Hilbert polynomial. Apply semi-continuity (cohomology and base change, [Hartshorne], III.12 / [Stacks Project], tag 02KH for the \(H^0\)-version) on the noetherian \(V_i\) to obtain a uniform integer \(N_1\) with \(R^r \pi _* \mathcal{F}(m) = 0\) for \(r \ge 1\), \(m \ge N_1\), and \(H^r(\mathbb {P}^n_s, \mathcal{F}_s(m)) = 0\) for all \(s \in S\), \(r \ge 1\), \(m \ge N_1\) (statement (B) of Nitsure’s proof). Choose \(r_i \ge N_1\) on each \(V_i\) such that the base-change comparison \((\pi _* \mathcal{F}(m))|_{V_i} \to (\pi _i)_* \mathcal{F}_{V_i}(m)\) is an isomorphism for \(m \ge r_i\); composing with the cohomology-and-base-change isomorphism \(((\pi _i)_* \mathcal{F}_{V_i}(m))|_s \xrightarrow {\sim } H^0(\mathbb {P}^n_s, \mathcal{F}_s(m))\) for the flat family on \(V_i\) yields uniform \(N = \max r_i\) such that \((\pi _* \mathcal{F}(m))|_s \to H^0(\mathbb {P}^n_s, \mathcal{F}_s(m))\) is an isomorphism for \(m \ge N\) and all \(s \in S\) (statement (C)).

    blueprint/web/chap-Picard_FlatteningStratification.html:2368:

    The Hilbert-polynomial-coincidence locus \(|W_f|\) may have non-flat scheme structure; refine to \(S_f \subseteq W_f\) by intersecting with the closed-subscheme conditions “\(\pi _* \mathcal{F}(N+i)|_{W_f}\) is locally-free of rank \(f(N+i)\)” for all \(i \ge 0\). These conditions are cut out by an increasing chain of coherent ideal sheaves \(I_0 \subseteq I_0 + I_1 \subseteq \cdots \) on \(W_f\); Noetherianity terminates the chain in finitely many steps, defining a coherent ideal sheaf \(I\) and a closed subscheme \(S_f \subseteq W_f\) with \(|S_f| = |W_f|\) on which \(\pi _* \mathcal{F}(N+i)\) is locally-free of rank \(f(N+i)\) for all \(i \ge 0\). The base-change-without-flatness lemma (cf. [Nitsure], §3) yields some \(N' \ge N\) such that for \(i \ge N'\), \((\pi _* \mathcal{F}(i))|_{S_f} \to (\pi _{S_f})_* \mathcal{F}_{S_f}(i)\) is an isomorphism, hence the graded \(A\)-module \(\bigoplus _{i \ge N'} (\pi _{S_f})_* \mathcal{F}_{S_f}(i)\) is locally-free on \(S_f\), hence \(\mathcal{F}_{S_f}\) is flat over \(S_f\). The closure-of-strata property (iii) reduces to the corresponding property in the \(n=0\) case for \(\pi _* \mathcal{F}(p)\) on \(S\) at any \(p \ge N\) separating all Hilbert polynomials.

    Source: [Nitsure], §4 (part (ii) of the main theorem); cf. [Stacks Project], tag 052H. Let \(S\), \(\mathcal{F}\), and \(\{ S_f\} _{f \in I}\) be as in 583. Set \(S' := \coprod _{f \in I} S_f\) with the coproduct morphism \(i : S' \to S\) assembled from the locally-closed inclusions. Then \(i^* \mathcal{F}\) is flat over \(S'\), and the pair \((S', i)\) is universal: for any morphism \(\varphi : T \to S\) of noetherian schemes (one may take \(T\) arbitrary, the Noetherian hypothesis on \(S\) being preserved), the pullback \(\varphi ^* \mathcal{F}\) on \(\mathbb {P}^n_T\) is \(T\)-flat if and only if \(\varphi \) factors uniquely through \(i\). In particular each \(S_f\) is uniquely determined by \(f\).
